title: Havenly acquires Burrow
content: Though her house of brands is growing, it’s not quite ready for sale. Like Burrow, Havenly has raised tens of millions in venture capital money—not to mention the equity doled out during its various acquisition deals—and has its own investors to please. But Mayer says the market conditions for an IPO aren’t right, and the company isn’t ready to be sold to a strategic buyer or private equity firm. “At least over the next couple of years, our perspective is to get as scaled and as profitable and [...] “Burrow’s innovative approach to design, in-home furniture delivery and functionality helped reinvent the way people furnish their homes, making it a natural fit for the Havenly family,” said Havenly CEO Lee Mayer in a statement accompanying the release. “Burrow fills a unique gap in the market and within our portfolio.” [...] The deal also formalizes what has long been clear: Havenly is an e-design brand in origin story only. Fees for design services only make up a tiny share of its overall revenue. And while design projects do drive significant sales for the company and its brands (Mayer pegged the number at 25 to 30 percent), they will likely influence a smaller and smaller percentage of its business as the overall pie grows bigger.
